# Mukta Arts

> Mukta Arts Limited is an Indian entertainment company founded by filmmaker Subhash Ghai in Mumbai in 1978. It is the group behind films such as Karz, Hero, Karma, Ram Lakhan, Saudagar, Khalnayak, Pardes and Taal, and it runs Whistling Woods International (film and creative arts education), Mukta A2 Cinemas (cinema exhibition) and SGM Studios (animation).

Mukta Arts was the first Hindi film company to list on the Indian stock exchanges, in 2000. Its headquarters is Mukta House, Film City Complex, Goregaon (East), Mumbai 400065, India. Official website: https://www.muktaarts.com

## Key facts

- Founded: 1978, by Subhash Ghai (Founder and Executive Chairman)
- Legal name: Mukta Arts Limited, a listed company (IPO in 2000)
- Films: 50+ films produced and co-produced, in Hindi and regional languages (Marathi, Bengali, Punjabi, Kannada), 35 blockbusters
- National Film Award: Iqbal (2005), Best Film on Other Social Issues
- Group companies: Mukta Arts Productions (films), Whistling Woods International (education, founded 2006), Mukta A2 Cinemas (exhibition), SGM Studios (animation)

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.muktaarts.com/): Overview of the Mukta Arts group and its four businesses.
- [About](https://www.muktaarts.com/about): History and milestones since 1978, board of directors, and investor relations documents (annual reports, annual returns, shareholding pattern, corporate governance, AGM notices).
- [Subhash Ghai](https://www.muktaarts.com/subhash-ghai): Profile of the founder. Writer-director of 19 films, 14 of them blockbusters; introduced India's first film insurance policy (CineMukta, through Taal); honours include Filmfare Best Director (Saudagar), Filmfare Best Screenplay (Pardes) and the IIFA Outstanding Contribution to Indian Cinema award (2015).
- [Mukta Arts Productions](https://www.muktaarts.com/our-films): The full film list with release years.
- [Whistling Woods International](https://www.muktaarts.com/whistling-woods): Film, media and creative arts institute in Film City, Mumbai, founded in 2006. Seven schools: Filmmaking, Media & Communication, Actors' Studio, Music, Design, Animation & Game Design, Fashion & Costume Design; plus an MBA in Creative Industries with IIM Mumbai and short courses. Official site: https://www.whistlingwoods.net/
- [Mukta A2 Cinemas](https://www.muktaarts.com/mukta-a2-cinemas): The exhibition arm, offering quality cinema at affordable prices in metro, Tier II and Tier III markets, including New Excelsior (Mumbai), Konark Theatre (Hyderabad), Ratnanjali (Ahmedabad) and Orbit Plaza (Surat), plus cinemas in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia. Official site: https://muktaa2cinemas.in/
- [SGM Studios](https://www.muktaarts.com/sgm-studios): The animation and visual storytelling arm, developing original, culturally rooted IP for film, series and new-age entertainment.
- [Submit Script](https://www.muktaarts.com/submit-script): How writers can submit an original, SWA-registered feature film or web series screenplay to Mukta Arts.

## Films by Mukta Arts

Kalicharan (1976), Vishwanath (1978), Gautam Govinda (1979), Karz (1980), Krodhi (1981), Vidhaata (1982), Hero (1983), Meri Jung (1985), Karma (1986), Uttar Dakshin (1987), Ram Lakhan (1989), Saudagar (1991), Prem Deewane (1992), Pyar Ki Ganga Bahe (1993), Khalnayak (1993), Trimurti (1995), Jaan (1996), Pardes (1997), Shyam Ghanshyam (1998), Taal (1999), Rahul (2001), Yaadein (2001), Badhaai Ho Badhaai (2002), Ek Aur Ek Gyarah (2003), Jogger’s Park (2003), Aitraaz (2004), Kisna (2005), Iqbal (2005), Shaadi Se Pehle (2006), 36 China Town (2006), Apna Sapna Money Money (2006), Good Boy Bad Boy (2007), Bombay to Bangkok (2008), Valu (2008), Black and White (2008), Sanai Choughade (2008), Yuvvraaj (2008), Paying Guests (2009), Right Yaaa Wrong (2010), Hello Darling (2010), Nouka Dubi / Kashmakash (2011), Love Express (2011), Cycle Kick (2011), Samhita (2013), Nimbehuli (2014), Kaanchi (2014), Double Di Trouble (2014), Vijeta (2020), Gandhi: A Perspective (2020), 36 Farmhouse (2022), Jaanki (2023), Tu Me Ani Amaira (2025)
